text:
alex: quick question — for gRPC bidi streams, do we want the gateway to hold a per-request retry budget or split it between frontdoor and upstream?

marta: my gut: split. frontdoor keeps 1 fast hedge, upstream gets the rest. avoids double-spending when upstream already retried.

sam: agreed on splitting but we need clear ownership for deadline propagation. if frontdoor hedges, it must annotate which attempt is primary for tracing + billing.

alex: +1 on annotation. want telemetry to show which attempt delivered final response. otherwise ops can't blame the right pool.

ops-bot: deploy-check: gateway/ingress v3.4.1 deployed to canary cluster at 1776543000 :rocket:

jia: small but important corner: what happens to in-flight KV cache for long-lived streams when a hedge attempt races? we could duplicate KV state and risk memory blowup.

ben: we should avoid full duplicate. proposal: keep a shared KV reference and fork only read-only pointers; any attempt that writes must coordinate via a lightweight sequencer (single writer).

marta: sequencing adds latency. alternative: forbid write-side-effects on hedged attempts; only the primary can commit side-effects. then hedged attempts are read-only and can be cancelled after finalization.

sam: that matches safety model we use elsewhere. implies we need a clear idempotency contract in the API for clients who expect side-effects during streams. document it.

alex: another related point: trailers and final status. if a hedged attempt finishes with trailers but the primary wins later with different trailers, which do we surface? we currently show first-successful, but that can hide final upstream finalizers.

jia: suggestion: merge metadata heuristically: prefer primary's trailers for authoritative side-effect status, but expose earliest progress trailers as events in progress stream for clients (non-authoritative). something like `progress-trailer:` events.

ben: we should include a boolean in our trace logs: `frontdoor.attempt_role = primary|hedge|probe`. that would make postmortems much easier.

marta: ok so summary of decisions proposed: 1) split retry budget (frontdoor 1 hedge + fallback token), 2) annotate attempts with role + attempt_id, 3) hedged attempts are read-only for side-effects, 4) primary's trailers are canonical, but we emit progress trailers as events, 5) don't duplicate KV memory, use shared read-only refs.

sam: implementation note: add headers `x-rw-attempt-id`, `x-rw-attempt-role`, and `x-rw-primary-deadline` to the proxy->upstream path. keep header forwarding opt-in per route for privacy.

alex: can someone make a short RFC followup with the header names + telemetry counters? want it by EOD so eng can start the canary.

marta: I'll draft it. will include a small state diagram for attempt lifecycle and memory ownership.

ben: pinging infra: we might need a tiny admission-control knob to cap concurrent hedges per tenant to avoid noisy neighbors.

ops-bot: incident-signal: added alert `ingress.hedge_count_per_tenant` threshold at 20 -> actions at 60s sustained.

jia: test plan idea: simulate a slow upstream that emits progressive trailers and ensure client sees progress events, then verify canonical trailers match primary. also assert no duplicated KV writes with chaos monkey.

sam: nice. and include a perf regression run for memory delta on long-lived streams (30m) with hedging on/off.

alex: thanks — sounds like we're converging. Marta, assign RFC number and drop in #architecture on your draft. I'll schedule a short review slot tomorrow 10:15. :+1:
